question.problem:
Let $R=[-3,-1]\times [1,3]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)=10-4x-2y.$
Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{1}=\{-3,-2,-1\},\,{P}_{2}=\{1,2,3\},\,P={P}_{1}\times {P}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate the upper Riemann sum $U(f,P).$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's draw the region $R$ and the partition $P.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14247841/assets/10eca85fc2ab60ea0b1ee229b0a0e20110f88c4724088c0f0630d22150a8a08d.png)

The upper sum $U(f,P)$ is given by

$$
U(f,P)={M}_{11}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{11})+{M}_{21}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{21})+{M}_{12}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{12})+{M}_{22}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{22}),
$$

where ${M}_{ij}$ is the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ We pick the *maximum* value of $f$ because we're finding the *upper* sum.

Taking into account the fact that $\text{Area}({R}_{ij})=1$ for all $4$ subregions, the formula for $U(f,P)$ reduces to

$$
U(f,P)={M}_{11}+{M}_{21}+{M}_{31}+{M}_{41}.
$$

Now, notice that

- $f(x,y)=10-4x-2y$ decreases as $x$ increases, and

- $f(x,y)=10-4x-2y$ decreases as $y$ increases.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14247841/assets/eaa3ed265eac5a53eedc07f07e2ff386505a6ea5cc4934653d587e84238b540d.png)

As a result, the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the *smallest* possible $x$ and the *smallest* possible $y.$ This is the value at the *bottom left corner* of each subregion.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14247841/assets/c332690fba1843ee09bd1466f1c978c41aff8438bf9b2a23a847ca58e2f9c228.png)

Hence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{11} & =f(-3,1)=20 \\ {M}_{21} & =f(-2,1)=16 \\ {M}_{12} & =f(-3,2)=18 \\ {M}_{22} & =f(-2,2)=14\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & =20+16+18+14 \\  & =68.\end{aligned}
$$
